references.text: In the preceding verse ([ref:Luk 22:35|Luke 22:35]), Jesus reminds the disciples of when he sent them out without a money bag, knapsack, or sandals, and they lacked nothing. Verse 36 marks a contrast – now the situation changes dramatically.

When Jesus sent out the seventy, he told them not to take a money bag, knapsack, or sandals ([ref:Luk 10:4|Luke 10:4]). In Luke 22:36, Jesus overturns this instruction and says they should now take both a money bag and a knapsack.

Also when the twelve were sent out, they were told not to take anything with them ([ref:Luk 9:3|Luke 9:3]). The contrast in 22:36 shows that a new time of opposition and persecution is about to begin.

Jesus' sending instructions in [ref:Matt 10:9-10|Matthew 10:9-10] forbid the disciples from taking gold, silver, a money bag, or extra clothes. Luke 22:36 reverses this for the new situation the disciples are about to face.

In the following verse ([ref:Luk 22:37|Luke 22:37]), Jesus explains why the situation is now different: Scripture concerning him must be fulfilled – he will be counted among lawbreakers. This provides the context for the drastic exhortation in verse 36.

The disciples' response in [ref:Luk 22:38|Luke 22:38] shows that they interpreted Jesus' words literally and presented two swords, whereupon Jesus said "It is enough". This reveals the tension in how the disciples understood Jesus' words about buying swords.

When one of the disciples actually used a sword in Gethsemane ([ref:Luk 22:49-51|Luke 22:49-51]), Jesus stopped him and healed the injured person. This suggests that the exhortation about the sword in verse 36 was not meant as an encouragement to armed resistance.
Jesus' words "put your sword back in its place" in [ref:Matt 26:52|Matthew 26:52] balance the exhortation in Luke 22:36 and show that Jesus did not want violent resistance.

The prophecy in [ref:Jes 53:12|Isaiah 53:12] that the Lord's servant will be counted among transgressors is quoted directly by Jesus in Luke 22:37 as the reason for the new instructions in verse 36. The sword underscores that Jesus will now be treated as a lawbreaker.

Paul's exhortation to put on the full armor of God and live in the light ([ref:Rom 13:12-14|Romans 13:12-14]) gives a spiritual dimension to the idea of being prepared for opposition – a theme that also underlies Jesus' words in Luke 22:36.

The exhortation to put on God's full armor, including "the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God" ([ref:Ef 6:13-17|Ephesians 6:13-17]), uses the sword metaphor spiritually and can shed light on the deeper meaning behind Jesus' words about buying a sword.
